question: Should experimental Claws be allowed to introduce arbitrary stdio MCP commands into the global MCP configuration, and if sharing is supported, what host authorization is required before another Claw can reuse that declaration?
rationale: This sets the execution and cross-role isolation contract. The existing code cannot safely choose whether to broker commands, scope resources, or permit global sharing without maintainer intent.

options.title: Require brokered, host-authorized MCP resources
options.body: Require a broker or explicit allowlist for stdio commands and an explicit host authorization record for any shared global MCP declaration before this lifecycle feature can merge.

options.title: Accept global manifest authority
options.body: Permit manifests to add arbitrary stdio commands and share exact global declarations, explicitly accepting the broader local execution and cross-role trust boundary.

options.title: Pause MCP ownership
options.body: Land no MCP lifecycle ownership behavior until the Claws RFC resolves command authority and global-resource isolation.

recommendation.title: Require brokered, host-authorized MCP resources
recommendation.body: Require a broker or explicit allowlist for stdio commands and an explicit host authorization record for any shared global MCP declaration before this lifecycle feature can merge.
